title: Cell Death Is a Genetic Program

scenes.visual: Title card: Cell Death Is a Genetic Program. Show a developing worm and a tissue with cell division balanced by cell removal.

scenes.tts: Why would a body kill its own cells? Death is a normal, genetically controlled part of building a body. Apoptosis uses caspases, proteins that cut other proteins. Cell loss balances the cells that are made. In the hermaphrodite worm, one hundred and thirty one cells die on schedule. The same cells die in every animal. In healthy tissue, dead cells are cleared so fast that you rarely see a corpse.

scenes.visual: Start with controlled cell removal during development, then balance cell division against cell loss in tissue. Show an invariant hermaphrodite worm lineage with the same 131 cells marked for death. End on prompt engulfment. Keep genetic control and normal tissue function prominent.

scenes.tts: But a repeated pattern does not prove a genetic program. The test is to change the genes. Without ced three or ced four, cells normally fated to die survive. Some even differentiate. The death itself has failed. Ced three turned out to be a caspase. Ced nine protects cells. Worm genetics had found the core of human death machinery. In apoptosis, cells shrink, their nuclei fragment, and their membranes stay intact until late.

scenes.visual: Compare the same identified cell in wild-type and ced-3 or ced-4 mutant worms: it dies in wild type but survives and differentiates in the mutant. Label CED-3 as a caspase and CED-9 as protective; do not draw a CED-9/CED-4 binding model. Bridge to a shrinking apoptotic cell with nuclear fragmentation and an intact membrane.

scenes.tts: Necrotic looks do not mean an accident. Swelling and rupture can also follow dedicated machinery. Necroptosis needs R I P K three and M L K L. Pyroptosis uses gasdermin pores. Ferroptosis depends on iron and severe lipid peroxidation. These are distinct regulated deaths. Appearance names an endpoint. To identify the cause, perturb the machinery and see whether the death changes.

scenes.visual: Show a swollen, rupturing cell as a shared appearance, then three separate mechanism cards: necroptosis, RIPK3 to MLKL; pyroptosis, gasdermin pores; ferroptosis, iron-dependent lipid peroxidation. Keep the routes separate. Finish with a machinery perturbation paired with a death readout, emphasizing a causal test rather than classification by appearance.

scenes.tts: Now follow the cleanup. A dying cell calls a phagocyte with find me signals. Caspases open channels that release nucleotides. The cell also exposes phosphatidylserine, a lipid normally kept inside its membrane. That is an eat me signal. A phagocyte recognizes the cell, engulfs it, and digests it in lysosomes. In culture, without a phagocyte, apoptotic cells generally become leaky. That is secondary necrosis.

scenes.visual: Show caspase-opened PANX1 releasing nucleotides to attract a phagocyte. Move phosphatidylserine from the inner to the outer membrane leaflet, then show recognition, engulfment into a phagosome, fusion with lysosomes and digestion. Omit the specialized Tim4/MerTK receptor division. Contrast with an unengulfed apoptotic cell in culture that later becomes leaky.

scenes.tts: How do we measure these events? Annexin five binds phosphatidylserine that is reachable from outside. Propidium iodide is a D N A dye. Its entry means the membrane is leaky. Neither marker tells you what killed the cell. Cells positive for both could be late apoptotic or necrotic from the start.

scenes.visual: Reuse blue annexin V and orange PI symbols. Show annexin V reporting accessible phosphatidylserine and PI entering a leaky cell to stain DNA. A compact annexin V/PI plot shows late apoptotic and primary necrotic cells reaching the same double-positive quadrant. Remove synthetic counts and the drug/time setup.

scenes.tts: So combine markers and follow them in time. Apoptotic cells expose the lipid before they leak. But necroptotic cells can do that too. A time course helps; it cannot settle the mechanism alone. One marker reports one event. Genetic control, distinct machinery, and clearance explain the biology behind the signal.

scenes.visual: Show an apoptotic trajectory through annexin-positive/PI-negative to double-positive, and note that necroptotic cells can also expose phosphatidylserine before leaking. Label the time course as informative but insufficient alone. End on the biological spine: genetic program, distinct execution machinery, recognition and clearance; complementary measurements sit beneath it.
End card: Cell Death and Clearance. Reprise genetic control, distinct machinery and prompt clearance, with the smaller assay panel beneath.
